The Pennsylvania State Employees Retirement System (SERS) is responsible for managing the public pension system for state employees in Pennsylvania, which currently has over a quarter of a million members in its retirement system[3]. SERS ensures that the pension earned by individuals is calculated accurately and arrives on time, offering support and assistance through various channels, including a helpline at 1.800.633.5461[5].

### Source 5:
At SERS, it's our job to make sure that the pension you've earned and the monthly payment option you've selected is calculated accurately and arrives on time - so you can do other things you want and need to do. If you like, you can print the 2023 payment calendar to keep. If you ever have questions, we're here to help. Please just call 1.800.633.5461.

Even though you're busy, it's important to take time to provide SERS with up-to-date information when your life changes:
- Reduce the possibility of lost or stolen checks by signing up for direct deposit
- Make sure the mailing address we have for you is accurate, even if you use direct deposit
- Keep your beneficiary designation current, if applicable
- Change your designated survivor, if the person you originally designated dies before you do, or if you get divorced or married
- Update the dependents on your REHP health coverage, if necessary
- Monitor and adjust your federal tax withholding, if you need to
- Tell us if your pension becomes part of a divorce or child support order
- Ensure that we have a fully executed power of attorney, if appropriate
It's also helpful to read your SERS newsletter and review your annual statement when it's mailed to you each January or when you sign in to SERS online member services. You can also sign up to have retired member updates sent to you by e-mail.

### Source 3:
What do flowers symbolize? We created a quick guide to 50 kinds of flowers and their meanings, with some unexpected surprises — for instance, did you know that the gladiolus is a flower that represents strength and the water lily represents enlightenment and purity? Throughout history, the symbolic meanings of flowers have changed and shifted. For instance, there are many ways to interpret a beautiful lily: In the Roman era, it was stuffed into pillows, so the lily often represented love; in the Middle Ages, it became a religious symbol representing purity; but today, they’re often used in funerals. Common flowers like the peony or the daisy are still loaded with meaning, too. The language of flowers became popular during the Victorian era, when outward shows of affection were frowned upon but lovers still wanted to express how they felt. We’ve taken a deeper look at the etymology to find some of the most surprising and interesting different flower meanings. Use our flower symbolism chart to figure out which flower will say what you want to convey!

strategyDetails.generatedAnswer: Flowers hold deep symbolic meanings across various cultures and time periods. For instance, the gladiolus symbolizes strength, while the water lily represents enlightenment and purity [3]. In the Victorian era, the language of flowers became popular as a way to express emotions subtly [3]. The meanings of flowers have evolved over time; for example, the lily has represented love, purity, and is now commonly used in funerals [3]. Each flower carries a unique significance, like the amaryllis symbolizing love, beauty, and determination [2]. Different flowers convey different emotions – from the red carnation representing deep romantic love to the white symbolizing innocence and pure love [1]. Understanding flower symbolism can add depth and sentiment to the act of giving flowers, making it a thoughtful and meaningful gesture [3].

What do flowers symbolize? We created a quick guide to 50 kinds of flowers and their meanings, with some unexpected surprises — for instance, did you know that the gladiolus is a flower that represents strength and the water lily represents enlightenment and purity? Throughout history, the symbolic meanings of flowers have changed and shifted. For instance, there are many ways to interpret a beautiful lily: In the Roman era, it was stuffed into pillows, so the lily often represented love; in the Middle Ages, it became a religious symbol representing purity; but today, they’re often used in funerals. Common flowers like the peony or the daisy are still loaded with meaning, too. The language of flowers became popular during the Victorian era, when outward shows of affection were frowned upon but lovers still wanted to express how they felt. We’ve taken a deeper look at the etymology to find some of the most surprising and interesting different flower meanings. Use our flower symbolism chart to figure out which flower will say what you want to convey!

What do flowers symbolize? We created a quick guide to 50 kinds of flowers and their meanings, with some unexpected surprises — for instance, did you know that the gladiolus is a flower that represents strength and the water lily represents enlightenment and purity? Throughout history, the symbolic meanings of flowers have changed and shifted. For instance, there are many ways to interpret a beautiful lily: In the Roman era, it was stuffed into pillows, so the lily often represented love; in the Middle Ages, it became a religious symbol representing purity; but today, they’re often used in funerals. Common flowers like the peony or the daisy are still loaded with meaning, too. The language of flowers became popular during the Victorian era, when outward shows of affection were frowned upon but lovers still wanted to express how they felt. We’ve taken a deeper look at the etymology to find some of the most surprising and interesting different flower meanings. Use our flower symbolism chart to figure out which flower will say what you want to convey!

strategyDetails.generatedAnswer: Flower symbolism has a rich history, with nearly every sentiment being expressed through flowers. For example, the amaryllis symbolizes pride and pastoral poetry, while the anemone signifies being forsaken [1]. Flowers like the aster are associated with love and daintiness, while the azalea conveys messages of temperance and fragile passion [1][2]. The carnation, with its various colors, can represent fascination, deep romantic love, or even rejection [1][2]. The language of flowers has evolved over time, with different interpretations for each bloom. In Victorian times, flowers were used to convey emotions when direct expressions of affection were discouraged [3]. Today, flowers like the gladiolus symbolize strength, while the water lily represents enlightenment and purity [3]. The symbolic meanings of flowers continue to be a fascinating aspect of human expression and communication [3].

### Source 3:
What do flowers symbolize? We created a quick guide to 50 kinds of flowers and their meanings, with some unexpected surprises — for instance, did you know that the gladiolus is a flower that represents strength and the water lily represents enlightenment and purity? Throughout history, the symbolic meanings of flowers have changed and shifted. For instance, there are many ways to interpret a beautiful lily: In the Roman era, it was stuffed into pillows, so the lily often represented love; in the Middle Ages, it became a religious symbol representing purity; but today, they’re often used in funerals. Common flowers like the peony or the daisy are still loaded with meaning, too. The language of flowers became popular during the Victorian era, when outward shows of affection were frowned upon but lovers still wanted to express how they felt. We’ve taken a deeper look at the etymology to find some of the most surprising and interesting different flower meanings. Use our flower symbolism chart to figure out which flower will say what you want to convey!

What do flowers symbolize? We created a quick guide to 50 kinds of flowers and their meanings, with some unexpected surprises — for instance, did you know that the gladiolus is a flower that represents strength and the water lily represents enlightenment and purity? Throughout history, the symbolic meanings of flowers have changed and shifted. For instance, there are many ways to interpret a beautiful lily: In the Roman era, it was stuffed into pillows, so the lily often represented love; in the Middle Ages, it became a religious symbol representing purity; but today, they’re often used in funerals. Common flowers like the peony or the daisy are still loaded with meaning, too. The language of flowers became popular during the Victorian era, when outward shows of affection were frowned upon but lovers still wanted to express how they felt. We’ve taken a deeper look at the etymology to find some of the most surprising and interesting different flower meanings. Use our flower symbolism chart to figure out which flower will say what you want to convey!

What do flowers symbolize? We created a quick guide to 50 kinds of flowers and their meanings, with some unexpected surprises — for instance, did you know that the gladiolus is a flower that represents strength and the water lily represents enlightenment and purity? Throughout history, the symbolic meanings of flowers have changed and shifted. For instance, there are many ways to interpret a beautiful lily: In the Roman era, it was stuffed into pillows, so the lily often represented love; in the Middle Ages, it became a religious symbol representing purity; but today, they’re often used in funerals. Common flowers like the peony or the daisy are still loaded with meaning, too. The language of flowers became popular during the Victorian era, when outward shows of affection were frowned upon but lovers still wanted to express how they felt. We’ve taken a deeper look at the etymology to find some of the most surprising and interesting different flower meanings. Use our flower symbolism chart to figure out which flower will say what you want to convey!

### Source 3:
What do flowers symbolize? We created a quick guide to 50 kinds of flowers and their meanings, with some unexpected surprises — for instance, did you know that the gladiolus is a flower that represents strength and the water lily represents enlightenment and purity? Throughout history, the symbolic meanings of flowers have changed and shifted. For instance, there are many ways to interpret a beautiful lily: In the Roman era, it was stuffed into pillows, so the lily often represented love; in the Middle Ages, it became a religious symbol representing purity; but today, they’re often used in funerals. Common flowers like the peony or the daisy are still loaded with meaning, too. The language of flowers became popular during the Victorian era, when outward shows of affection were frowned upon but lovers still wanted to express how they felt. We’ve taken a deeper look at the etymology to find some of the most surprising and interesting different flower meanings. Use our flower symbolism chart to figure out which flower will say what you want to convey!

What do flowers symbolize? We created a quick guide to 50 kinds of flowers and their meanings, with some unexpected surprises — for instance, did you know that the gladiolus is a flower that represents strength and the water lily represents enlightenment and purity? Throughout history, the symbolic meanings of flowers have changed and shifted. For instance, there are many ways to interpret a beautiful lily: In the Roman era, it was stuffed into pillows, so the lily often represented love; in the Middle Ages, it became a religious symbol representing purity; but today, they’re often used in funerals. Common flowers like the peony or the daisy are still loaded with meaning, too. The language of flowers became popular during the Victorian era, when outward shows of affection were frowned upon but lovers still wanted to express how they felt. We’ve taken a deeper look at the etymology to find some of the most surprising and interesting different flower meanings. Use our flower symbolism chart to figure out which flower will say what you want to convey!

strategyDetails.generatedAnswer:
Flowers have been used to convey sentiments since ancient times. Each flower carries a unique meaning, allowing people to express a wide range of emotions. For example, the rose symbolizes love and beauty, while the daffodil represents new beginnings and chivalry [1][2][3].

In Victorian times, the language of flowers, or floriography, became popular as a way to communicate feelings subtly when outward displays of affection were frowned upon. For instance, the lily, which symbolized love in Roman times, transitioned to representing purity in the Middle Ages and is now often used at funerals [1][3].

Some common flowers and their meanings include the carnation, which signifies fascination and love, with different colors carrying distinct messages such as red for deep romantic love and white for innocence and purity [1][2][4]. The hydrangea, on the other hand, can convey frigidity negatively or heartfelt emotion positively, depending on the color [1][5].

Understanding the symbolism behind flowers can add depth and thoughtfulness to your gift-giving. So, the next time you present someone with a bouquet, consider the meanings behind the blooms you choose to express your sentiments effectively [1][3].

What do flowers symbolize? We created a quick guide to 50 kinds of flowers and their meanings, with some unexpected surprises — for instance, did you know that the gladiolus is a flower that represents strength and the water lily represents enlightenment and purity? Throughout history, the symbolic meanings of flowers have changed and shifted. For instance, there are many ways to interpret a beautiful lily: In the Roman era, it was stuffed into pillows, so the lily often represented love; in the Middle Ages, it became a religious symbol representing purity; but today, they’re often used in funerals. Common flowers like the peony or the daisy are still loaded with meaning, too. The language of flowers became popular during the Victorian era, when outward shows of affection were frowned upon but lovers still wanted to express how they felt. We’ve taken a deeper look at the etymology to find some of the most surprising and interesting different flower meanings. Use our flower symbolism chart to figure out which flower will say what you want to convey!

What do flowers symbolize? We created a quick guide to 50 kinds of flowers and their meanings, with some unexpected surprises — for instance, did you know that the gladiolus is a flower that represents strength and the water lily represents enlightenment and purity? Throughout history, the symbolic meanings of flowers have changed and shifted. For instance, there are many ways to interpret a beautiful lily: In the Roman era, it was stuffed into pillows, so the lily often represented love; in the Middle Ages, it became a religious symbol representing purity; but today, they’re often used in funerals. Common flowers like the peony or the daisy are still loaded with meaning, too. The language of flowers became popular during the Victorian era, when outward shows of affection were frowned upon but lovers still wanted to express how they felt. We’ve taken a deeper look at the etymology to find some of the most surprising and interesting different flower meanings. Use our flower symbolism chart to figure out which flower will say what you want to convey!

With over 14,000 locations in the United States, Domino's has even more stores than Pizza Hut. Famous for its garlic butter herb crust pizza, this restaurant offers so much more than just "za." Specialties include Buffalo wings, gooey stuffed cheesy bread and even hearty Italian-style pasta. Check the hottest Domino's deals so you can feed a whole party for less.

As far as convenience goes, not much beats a fast pizza delivery from Domino's. You can also pick up your order to save on delivery fees. For even greater convenience, place your order online or through the Domino's app. Either way, make sure that you apply all applicable Domino's promo codes and coupons so you'll get the best value for your money.

Not every pickup and trip back home goes smoothly: Say a pothole on Main Street causes your pie to flip over or a guy in a pickup cuts in front of you and sends the pizza flying. No worries here, because Domino's has you covered for all those scenarios and more. Just head back to the restaurant where you got your food, and they'll be happy to make you a fresh pizza at no cost.

Domino's values loyalty with more of what you love. It's easy to start rewarding yourself when you join the Piece of the Pie rewards program:
- Sign up online with your email address
- Make a purchase of at least $10 to earn 10 points
- Earn 60 points and you'll get a free pizza

You can make up to one qualifying order per day. This program has the added benefit of allowing you to save your favorite orders to your profile so you can make them again whenever you like. You can even place your go-to order merely by sending a text containing a pizza emoji!

While Domino's prices are generally pretty reasonable, you can enjoy even greater savings by checking out the Deals tab at the top of the homepage. Click on See Local Coupons to display anything that's currently offered at your local store. After that, all you have to do is click Add Promo to Cart and you're ready to check out. Your Domino's offer will be applied and you'll see the subtotal drop.
